question: From the top of a building 15 m high, the angle of depression to a point on the ground is 45 degrees. Find the horizontal distance from the building to the point.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

In a right-angled triangle, if the angle of elevation/depression is 45°, then the Perpendicular and Base are always equal (Ratio 1 : 1).

Height of building (Perpendicular) = 15 m

Horizontal distance (Base) = Height of building

∴ Horizontal distance = 15 m

**∴ The correct answer is 15 m.**

**Given:**

Height of the building (AB) = 15 m

Angle of depression from top A to point C = 45°

Angle of elevation from point C to top A = 45° (Alternate interior angles)

**Formula Used:**

tan θ = Perpendicular / Base

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/61253a4323d3dfc3d816a63af1e0757f80c3fa5aa90c95107fa6e4ae5b0504f9.png] 

In right-angled triangle ABC:

⇒ tan 45° = AB / BC

⇒ 1 = 15 / BC

⇒ BC = 15 m

**∴ The correct answer is 15 m.**

Standard Trigonometric Ratios

For 30°, tan 30° = 1/√3; For 60°, tan 60° = √3. These are commonly used to find heights and distances.

Angle of Depression vs Elevation

The angle of depression from an observer to an object is numerically equal to the angle of elevation from the object to the observer due to parallel horizontal lines.

Pythagoras Theorem

In any right-angled triangle, Hypotenuse² = Perpendicular² + Base². In this case, AC = √(15² + 15²) = 15√2 m.
